a: A reading begins at 11:47 a.m. and ends at 12:26 p.m. Its only pause lasts 8 minutes. How many minutes are spent reading?
b: From 11:47 a.m. until 12:26 p.m., a narrator reads aloud except for one 8-minute break. How long does the narrator spend reading aloud, in minutes?

a: At a fair, 16 stalls sell mugs and 13 sell bowls. Five sell both. How many stalls sell exactly one of those two items?
b: A fair lists 16 mug sellers and 13 bowl sellers, with five stalls on both lists. How many stalls appear on just one list?

a: A bookbinder needs 47 blank sheets and has 12. Extra sheets come only in packs of eight. What is the fewest packs she must buy?
b: A binder has 12 of the 47 sheets a book requires. How many whole packs of eight would just cover the shortfall, allowing leftover sheets?

a: A potter fires a cup, a bowl, a jug and a tray one at a time. The tray goes last, and the cup goes before the jug. How many firing orders are possible?
b: A tray closes a firing schedule whose first three slots hold a bowl, a jug and a cup in some order. How many schedules put the jug later than the cup?
proof: Half the 3! permutations of the first three objects place the cup before the jug.
